Here’s a quick recap of the top stories.
SK Hynix’s Solidigm Explores $150 Billion IPO
South Korean memory giant SK Hynix Inc.’s U.S. subsidiary
Solidigm

is reportedly considering an initial public offering (IPO) as early as next year. The NAND flash and storage unit could be valued at up to $150 billion. Solidigm met with investment banks this week in a competitive "bake-off" for IPO roles, according to sources.
Nvidia’s GPU Demand Through the Roof

The demand for NVIDIA Corp.’s GPUs has become so intense that even cloud providers with poorly functioning infrastructure can still find customers willing to pay healthy margins. “If you’ve got GPUs," buyers will pay, says researcher Sam Harshe, even if a provider’s Kubernetes is "completely broken" and its storage "barely works."

children: AMD Stock Hits 52-Week High
Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
‘s stock rose more than 2% in Friday’s premarket trading as technology stocks gained alongside a broader improvement in risk appetite. Nasdaq futures rose 0.55%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.33%.
Disney+ Subscription Prices Nearly Doubled Since 2023
Walt Disney Co.’s
Disney+ and
Hulu

subscribers in the U.S. face another round of price increases as Disney raises ad-free plans and several bundles and continues to push customers toward multi-service subscriptions. Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium, both of which offer ad-free streaming, are increasing 13% to $21.49 per month, up $2.50 from $18.99.
OpenAI AI Agent Bypasses Australian Government Health Portal Security
An
OpenAI
AI agent bypassed security restrictions on an Australian government health portal in June while researching public healthcare spending. Australian Prime Minister
Anthony Albanese
said the AI agent gained unauthorized access to files on a Medicare medical statistics portal.
